tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (symptoms the user describes like slowness, alarms firing, modification requests) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including non-obvious phrasing ('even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower'), and explicitly excludes out-of-scope domains (S3, EFS, FSx, instance store). It is a longer paragraph but remains focused and justified given the breadth of the skill's scope.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on EBS-specific domain knowledge (metric names, binding layers, modification limits) without explaining generic concepts the agent already knows. It is dense but each sentence carries domain-specific signal.
tests.evidence: Use this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account's Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (metric thresholds, API lists, report formats) is consistently delegated to references/ files; the body only contains routing tables, critical rules, and gotchas summaries rather than large data blocks.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link format in the body (data-collection.md, ebs-best-practices.md, finding-logic.md, metrics-thresholds.md, review-operational.md, review-report-format.md, troubleshoot-billing.md, troubleshoot-encryption.md, troubleshoot-performance.md, troubleshoot-snapshots.md, troubleshoot-volume-modification.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the classification table and workflow steps is tied to a specific trigger condition or purpose, clearly indicating when to load it.
tests.evidence: "My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md]

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (modification limits, deletion rules, approval requirements) are stated with exact prescriptive language, while flexible areas (classification table, escalation) explain purpose and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours... AWS DevOps Agent refuses delete-class operations

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tool options; it routes to specific reference procedures per scenario rather than offering multiple equal approaches for the same task.
tests.evidence: The classification table maps each scenario to exactly one reference path, e.g. "Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md]"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable classification-then-procedure approach applicable to any EBS issue, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the Request ... Step 3: Run the Path and Draft the Report

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to EBS behavior.
tests.evidence: A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill references dedicated report format files (review-report-format.md, finding-logic.md) for its structured outputs rather than omitting templates.
tests.evidence: Review mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The troubleshoot verdict format listed in the body is a short 6-item list, well under 20 lines, and the larger review report template is offloaded to references/review-report-format.md.
tests.evidence: 1. **Answer:** ... 6. **Gaps:** what could not be checked and why.
